newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes weaker, Oman premium off sharply.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes weaker, Oman premium off sharply.

text.p: Asian crude felt the weight of refinery run cuts and weaker demand on Tuesday, as prices fell further, traders said.
The biggest price losses appeared in the Oman market where one Japanese trader sold a cargo to China at MPM +11 cents.
A second deal was talked at MPM +11 cents, but traders said they believed it was a Japanese trader selling to an affiliate.
Another deal was confirmed at MPM +18 cents on Monday and one at MPM +20 on Friday.
Last week Oman deals were talked at MPM +27 to +29 cents, although some players said the latest deals were overdone.
They put the Oman market at 15 to 20 cents, rather than below 15 cents.
The price slide was further reflected in the Middle East market where a European major sold a cargo of Murban to a Japanese refiner at ADNOC +30 cents, down five cents from a deal late last week.
The same major sold Qatar Marine at QGPC +20 cents, also down five cents from the last deal. Lower Zakum was heard done at ADNOC +35 cents, holding previous premiums.
Three refiners in Singapore have decided to cut runs against a backdrop of weak margins.
Japanese runs were lower as the sector alters schedules for spring, traders said.
The regional market was finding more support with most Indonesia grades holding premium levels.
A Pertamina affiliate was said to have sold 200,000 barrels of Minas at ICP +$1.20/$1.25 and a another deal, with specific dates attached, was heard at ICP +$1.30 -- all in line with recent deals.
